rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted “it is said” introduces the command, which functions circumstantially with the criminal’s wish in 69:25.
rows.anchor: مقول لقول محذوف موقعه في موقع الحال من ضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ones ordered to seize him are the angels assigned to drive the judged toward their destination.
rows.anchor: ومعلوم من المقام أن المأمورين بأن يأخذوه هم الملائكة الموكلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking him means gripping him by hand.
rows.anchor: والأخذ : الإمساك باليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to put him in a neck shackle used for an offender or captive.
rows.anchor: غلوه : أمر من غله إذا وضعه في الغل وهو القيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is derived from a noun and is attested only in the triliteral form; its expected doubled form may have been shortened for ease.
rows.anchor: فلعلهم قالوا : غله تخفيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prefixed fa conveys speed: shackling follows immediately after the seizure.
rows.anchor: وعطف بفاء التعقيب لإفادة الإسراع بوضعه في الأغلال عقب أخذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first thumma marks a higher rank of punishment: entering the Fire is harsher than seizure and shackling.
rows.anchor: للتراخي الرتبي لأن مضمون الجملة المعطوفة بها أشد في العقاب من أخذه ووضعه في الأغلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣallā the Fire means to suffer its burning or warm oneself by it; when made transitive it takes the forms aṣlāhu nāran or ṣallāhu nāran.
rows.anchor: مضاعف تضعيف تعدية لأن صلي النار معناه أصابه حرقها أو تدفأ بها

words: ثم في سلسلة ذرعها سبعون ذراعا فاسلكوه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second thumma ranks the seventy-cubit chain above the preceding punishments; inserting him into it is worse than merely putting him in Hell.
rows.anchor: للتراخي الرتبي بالنسبة لمضمون الجملتين قبلها لأن مضمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Make him enter the chain by wrapping it around him so that he is inside it, bound in the Fire.
rows.anchor: اجعلوه سالكا ، أي داخلا في السلسلة وذلك بأن تلف عليه السلسلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting “Hell” and “in a chain” hastens the hearer’s distress and maintains the rhyme.
rows.anchor: على عامله لتعجيل المساءة مع الرعاية على الفاصلة وكذلك تقديم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa either reinforces the fa in “shackle him” or makes this command resemble the answer to an omitted condition signaled by the fronted phrase.
rows.anchor: وإما للايذان بأن الفعل منزل منزلة جزاء شرط محذوف ، وهذا الحذف يشعر به تقديم المعمول غالبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the promised event “far” insinuates impossibility because disbelievers reject its occurrence, and sows doubt among believers, as in their earlier claim.
rows.anchor: هنا كناية عن معنى الإحالة لأنهم لا يؤمنون بوقوع العذاب الموعود به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Near” is a figurative assertion that the event will certainly occur, with anticipatory matching and emphasis.
rows.anchor: كناية عن تحقق الوقوع على طريق المشاكلة التقديرية والمبالغة في التحقق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairing of “far” and “near” is antithesis.
rows.anchor: وبين { بعيدا } و { قريبا } محسن الطباق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day-clause can attach to “ascend” in 70:4, or to “the criminal wishes,” placed later for emphasis on the Day.
rows.anchor: قدم عليه للاهتمام بذكر اليوم فيكون قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If “the day when the sky…” opens a new sentence, it is an embedded-subject substitute for the no-question statement: terror causes the failure to ask, and the criminal’s wish to ransom is part of that scene.
rows.anchor: لأن عدم المساءلة مسبب عن شدة الهول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muhl means the dregs of oil.
rows.anchor: و { المهل } : دردي الزيتت . والمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is likened to oil as its constituent parts dissolve, as in the image of the sky becoming a rose like oil in 55:37.
rows.anchor: وهذا كقوله في سورة الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿihn is glossed as dyed wool, either dyed in general or dyed in many colors; al-Rāghib and al-Zamakhsharī follow the multicolored reading.
rows.anchor: قيل المصبوغ ألوانا مختلفة وهو الذي درج عليه الراغب والزمخشري

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr’s line compares wool fragments at each campsite to scattered al-fanā berries, supporting the image of colored wool.
rows.anchor: قال زهير : كان فتات العهن في كل منزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-fanā, also called ʿinab al-thaʿlab, is a wild berry that appears green, yellow, and red; al-ʿahana is a desert plant with a red flower.
rows.anchor: وله ألوان بعضه أخضر وبعضه أصفر وبعضه أحمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wool simile conveys the mountains’ dispersed parts as the world’s structure dissolves, matching the image in 101:5.
rows.anchor: ووجه الشبه بالعهن تفرق الأجزاء كما جاءت في آية القارعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wool is chosen to complete the resemblance because mountains have varied colors, as 35:27 says of their white and red streaks.
rows.anchor: لإكمال المشابهة لأن الجبال ذات ألوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky and mountains take these forms as their cohesion dissolves at the end of this world and the transition to the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: حين ينحل تماسك أجزائهما عند انقراض هذا العالم والمصير إلى عالم الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Friends do not ask after each other because terror leaves each occupied with his own distress, even while he sees his close friend suffering.
rows.anchor: فمن شدة ذلك أن يرى الحميم حميمه في كرب وعناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of “ask” is omitted because its meaning—asking about the friend’s condition—is clear from context and from their seeing one another.
rows.anchor: أي يبصر الأخلاء أحوال أخلائهم من الكرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminal would offer everyone on earth as ransom, including beloved companions, relatives, and precious possessions people normally cling to; compare 3:91.
rows.anchor: مما يعز عليه من أخلاء وقرابة ونفائس الأموال مما شأن الناس الشح ببذله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronoun man gives precedence to rational beings because the group includes close friends.
rows.anchor: لتغليب العاقل على غيره لأن منهم الأخلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second thumma marks rank: the hoped-for rescue matters most to the criminal, after he has wished to offer the ransom.
rows.anchor: للتراخي الرتبي ، أي يود بذل ذلك وأن ينجيه الفداء من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “save him” refers to the understood ransom, as in the pronoun in 5:8 referring to justice.
rows.anchor: عائد إلى الافتداء المفهوم من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although a result after wishing would more often take fa, thumma stresses the criminal’s intense concern to escape by any means; compare 4:89 and 68:9.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على شدة اهتمام المجرم بالنجاة بأية وسيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object of “save him” is supplied by the nearby phrase “from the punishment of that Day.”
rows.anchor: ومتعلق { ينجيه } محذوف يدل عليه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rejects the criminal’s imagined ransom, whether an unspoken wish known to God or a voiced hope; the estimate is: no ransom and no rescue.
rows.anchor: يقال له كلا ، أي لا افتداء ولا إنجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “It is a blaze” begins an explanatory resumption prompted by kalla’s rejection.
rows.anchor: استئناف بياني ناشىء عما أفاده حرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun refers to the sight of Hell that the criminal sees before him.
rows.anchor: عائد إلى ما يشاهده المجرم قبالته من مرأى جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun is feminine because laẓā has feminine alif; the following descriptions predicate further qualities of it.
rows.anchor: مقترنا بألف التأنيث أنث الضمير باعتبار تأنيث الخبر واتبع اسمها بأوصاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description implies that the blaze is prepared for the criminal: it burns him and strips away his scalp.
rows.anchor: أي أنها تحرقك وتنزع شواك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next verse makes the implied threat explicit: the Fire calls the one who rejected the call to monotheism, turned away, and cared only for hoarded wealth.
rows.anchor: وقد صرح بما وقع التعريض به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “It calls” is a second predicate with the nominative reading of “nazzāʿatan,” or a circumstantial clause under either reading.
rows.anchor: إما خبر ثان حسب قراءة { نزاعة } بالرفع وإما حال على القراءتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One nonliteral reading makes the Fire a host summoning guests to a banquet, a sarcastic personification cued by the description of its victims.
rows.anchor: شبهت لظى في انهيال الناس إليها بضائف لمأدبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading, tadʿū derives from the noun for an invitation, with the following description serving as a cue or elaboration.
rows.anchor: أي من أدبر وتولى عن الإيمان بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another figurative reading portrays the unbelievers’ gathering at the Fire as its invitation to attend, using a dependent comparison to a caller’s summons.
rows.anchor: أو أن يشبه إحضار الكفار عندها بدعوتها إياهم للحضور

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rummah’s line about a wild bull says that al-rabab plants “call” to its nose, cited for this figurative use of calling.
rows.anchor: كقول ذي الرمة يصف الثور الوحشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A literal reading takes the callers to be Hell’s angels, with the attribution to Hell by place or cause.
rows.anchor: و ( الذين يدعون ) : هم الملائكة الموكلون بجهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Hell itself calls literally when God creates voices in it summoning the rejecters, then devours them.
rows.anchor: بأن يخلق الله فيها أصواتا تنادي الذين تولوا أن يردوا عليها فتلتهمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description denotes the criminals who wish to ransom themselves from the punishment in 70:14.
rows.anchor: جنس الموصوفين بأنهم أدبروا وتولوا وجمعوا وهم المجرمون الذين يودون أن يفتدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are traits of polytheists and consequences of shirk: rejecting and turning away from Islam, and hoarding wealth out of fear for it.
rows.anchor: وهذه الصفات خصائص المشركين ، وهي من آثار دين الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adbara suggests turning one’s back from the outset; tawallā suggests leaving after having engaged, so the conjunction preserves a distinction rather than mere repetition.
rows.anchor: ففي التولي معنى إيثار غير المتولى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adbara depicts rejecting the Qur’an without listening from the beginning (41:26); tawallā depicts turning away after hearing it (8:31). Both states characterize the polytheists and warrant punishment.
rows.anchor: والتولي مستعار للإعراض عن القرآن بعد سماعه وللنفور عن دعوة الرسول

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf assigns both verbs the same object: turning away from the truth.
rows.anchor: وفي ( الكشاف ) : أدبر عن الحق وتولى عنه

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī assigns separate objects: he rejects truth, meaning faith, and turns from obedience after hearing the Messenger’s call.
rows.anchor: فقدر البيضاوي : أدبر عن الحق وتولى عن الطاعة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatādah reverses the objects: turning away from God’s obedience and from God’s Book; al-Fakhr and al-Nīsābūrī follow this view.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة عكسه : أدبر عن طاعة الله وتولى عن كتاب الله وتبعه الفخر والنيسابوري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence of gathering and then storing indicates that the omitted object of “gathered” is something put into a container.
rows.anchor: مرتب ثانيهما على أولهما ، فيدل ترتب الثاني على الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He gathered money, hoarded it, and did not benefit the needy; awa means to be miserly, supported by the hadith saying not to hoard lest it be hoarded against you.
rows.anchor: أي جمع المال فكنزه ولم ينفع به المحاويج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra is called al-Jinn in tafsīr works and manuscripts, by al-Tirmidhī, and popularly “Qul ūḥiya”; al-Bukhārī titles it “Sūrat Qul ūḥiya.” Both names are apt, though al-Itqān does not list it among multiply named sūras.
rows.anchor: في كتب التفسير وفي المصاحف التي رأيناها ومنها الكوفي المكتوب بالقيروان في القرن الخامس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra is Meccan by consensus.
rows.anchor: وهي مكية بالاتفاق . ويظهر أنها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report in the two Ṣaḥīḥs and al-Tirmidhī says the Prophet and companions headed toward the ʿUkāẓ market at Nakhlah; while he prayed dawn, jinn listened and returned to tell their people they had heard wondrous Qur’an.
rows.anchor: من حديث ابن عباس أنه قال : انطلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في طائفة من أصحابه

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq places the revelation after the Prophet’s trip to al-Ṭāʾif seeking support from Thaqīf, in the tenth year of the mission, three years before the Hijra.
rows.anchor: ذكر ابن إسحاق أن نزول هذه السورة كان بعد سفر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى الطائف يطلب النصرة من ثقيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra is the fortieth in revelation order, after al-Aʿrāf and before Yā-Sīn; scholars agree it has twenty-eight verses.
rows.anchor: وقد عدت السورة الأربعين في نزول السور نزلت بعد الأعراف وقبل يس

words: أوحي إلي أنه استمع نفر من الجن
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording implies that the Prophet learned of the jinn’s listening only through God’s revelation, not before the verse was sent down.
rows.anchor: إيماء إلى أنه ما علم بذلك إلا بإخبار الله إياه بوقوع هذا الاستماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ahqāf passage (46:29–30) may recall this event, or may refer to a separate story reported by Ibn Masʿūd in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim about recitation in prayers; Ibn Ashur says that story is unrelated to this verse.
rows.anchor: فتذكير بما في هذه الآية أو هي إشارة إلى قصة أخرى رواها عبد الله بن مسعود وهي في صحيح مسلم

words: أوحي إلي أنه استمع نفر من الجن
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause that a group listened is the passive subject of “it was revealed to me,” meaning that their listening was revealed to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: في موضع نائب فاعل { أوحي } أي أوحي إلي استماع نفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle anna emphasizes the revealed report because it is extraordinary.
rows.anchor: وتأكيد الخبر الموحى بحرف ( أن ) للاهتمام به لغرابته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in anna is a pronoun of the affair, with the following sentence as its predicate, further stressing the revelation.
rows.anchor: وضمير { أنه } ضمير الشأن وخبره جملة { استمع نفر من الجن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of “listened” is omitted and supplied by the jinn’s statement: they listened to the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: ومفعول { استمع } محذوف دل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafar means a group of one to ten; it normally denotes humans, but is analogically applied to jinn for lack of another word.
rows.anchor: النفر : الجماعة من واحد إلى عشرة وأصله في اللغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likewise, “men” in 72:6 denotes jinn persons, using a human term for them.
rows.anchor: كما أطلق رجال في قوله : { يعوذون برجال من الجن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They said this to members of their kind who were absent; God inspired them to warn and guide them, as elaborated in 46:29–30.
rows.anchor: قالوه لبعض منهم لم يحضر لاستماع القرآن ألهمهم الله أن ينذروهم ويرشدوهم إلى الصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They said” means conveying their intent in the mode by which they communicate, since jinn apparently do not use words spoken on tongues; it is a figurative use like the ant’s speech in 27:18.
rows.anchor: ومعنى القول هنا : إبلاغ مرادهم إلى من يريدون أن يبلغوه إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s metaphorical use of speech, like the ant’s communication in 27:18, dignifies Islam by giving it callers from both kinds of beings.
rows.anchor: فيكون ذلك تكريما لهذا الدين أن جعل الله له دعاة من الثقلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghadaq means abundant, plentiful water.
rows.anchor: الغدق : بفتح الغين المعجمة وفتح الدال الماء الغزير الكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause “to test them in it” is parenthetical between the conditional promise of water in 72:16 and the warning in 72:17.
rows.anchor: إدماج فهي معترضة بين جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional promise in 72:16 carries an indirect warning, made explicit here: if they turn away, their state becomes punishment and they are driven into its paths.
rows.anchor: ثم أكدت الكناية عن الإنذار المأخوذة من قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salk means to insert; the verb can be intransitive or transitive, as in al-Aʿshā’s line about a carpenter putting a nail into a door.
rows.anchor: والسلك : حقيقته الإدخال ، وفعله قاصر ومتعد

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s verse uses salk for inserting a nail into a door, illustrating the verb’s literal sense.
rows.anchor: قال الأعشى : كما سلك السكي في الباب فيتق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is extended by an uncommon metaphor to convey the force of the punishment: they will suffer an inescapable torment.
rows.anchor: واستعمل السلك هنا في معنى شدة وقوع الفعل على طريق الاستعارة وهي استعارة عزيزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAdhāban is accusative after omission of the preposition fī; its figurative containment pictures punishment surrounding its victim like a vessel surrounds its contents.
rows.anchor: وانتصب عذابا } على نزع الخافض وهو حرف الظرفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording shifts from a pronoun to “his Lord” to signal why the warning applies: one who turns from his Creator and Sustainer deserves punishment.
rows.anchor: والعدول عن الإضمار إلى الإظهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣaʿad means hard and overpowering, as if the punishment rises over and masters its victim; compare 44:19.
rows.anchor: والصعد : الشاق الغالب ، وكأنه جاء من مصدر صعد ، كفرح إذا علا وارتفع

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most readers recite naslukhu with the first-person plural “We insert him.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { نسلكه } بنون العظمة ففيه التفات

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب وخلف
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Yaʿqūb, and Khalaf recite yaslukhu with a third-person subject referring to the Lord.
rows.anchor: وقرأه عاصم وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب وخلف { يسلكه } بياء الغائب

rows.speaker: القراء العشرة
rows.claim: All ten readers open the hamza in “and the mosques belong to God.”
rows.anchor: اتفق القراء العشرة على فتح الهمزة في { وأن المساجد لله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause coordinates with the nominative clause about the jinn listening in 72:1, so its content too was revealed to the Prophet and commanded for him to say.
rows.anchor: ومضمونها مما أوحي به إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأمر بأن يقوله

words: وأنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه
rows.speaker: نافع وأبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Abū Bakr’s transmission from ʿĀṣim read the hamza in inna with kasra.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وحده وأبو بكر عن عاصم بكسر الهمزة

words: وأنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه
rows.speaker: بقية العشرة
rows.claim: The remaining readers in their well-known transmissions read the hamza with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وقرأه بقية العشرة في رواياتهم المشهورة بالفتح

words: وأنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both readings place the statement outside the jinn’s quotation and make it part of God’s revelation.
rows.anchor: ومآل القراءتين سواء في كون هذا خارجا عما صدر عن الجن وفي كونه مما أوحى الله به

words: وأنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra, the sentence coordinates with “it was revealed to me”; it means “say that when God’s servant stood calling Him,” since inna in quoted speech is kasra.
rows.anchor: فكسر الهمزة على عطف الجملة على جملة

words: وأنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It cannot be treated as the jinn’s continuing speech: their report had ended and the passage had moved to other subjects beginning at 72:18.
rows.anchor: ولا يليق أن يجعل من حكاية مقالة الجن لأن ذلك قد انقضى وتباعد

words: وأنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa, the clause coordinates with the revelation that the jinn listened; God revealed that the polytheists nearly crowded around His servant as he prayed.
rows.anchor: وأما الفتح فعلى اعتباره معطوفا على جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in inna is a pronoun of the affair, with the clause beginning “when God’s servant stood” as its predicate.
rows.anchor: وضمير { إنه } ضمير الشأن وجملة { لما قام عبد الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns “they” refer to the polytheists, who are suggested by the context from 72:16 through the prohibition in 72:18.
rows.anchor: وضمير { كادوا يكونون } عائدان إلى المشركين المنبىء عنهم المقام غيبة وخطابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “God’s servant” is Muhammad; the explicit title replaces an expected pronoun to honor him through the ennobling association of servitude to God, as in 17:1.
rows.anchor: و { عبد الله } هو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وضع الاسم الظاهر موضع المضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lubadan is a collective noun for a mass whose parts are felted together, like the thick mane of a lion.
rows.anchor: { ولبدا } بكسر اللام وفتح الموحدة اسم جمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists nearly crowded tightly around Muhammad to hear his recitation and call to monotheism, gathering in anger and intent on harm.
rows.anchor: كاد المشركون يكونون مثل اللبد متراصين مقتربين منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāma can mean striving in the call to God, as in the youths who stood and declared their faith in 18:14.
rows.anchor: اجتهد في الدعوة إلى الله ، كقوله تعالى :

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nābighah’s line about the sons of Asad standing and proclaiming their protection illustrates qāma as taking a public stand and speaking.
rows.anchor: وقال النابغة : بأن حصنا وحيا من بني أسد قاموا فقالوا

rows.speaker: جزء بن كليب الفقعسي
rows.claim: The line by Juzʾ ibn Kulayb al-Faqʿasī uses the Prophet’s rising as the start of his public worship of God alone.
rows.anchor: قال جزء بن كليب الفقعسي : فلا تبغينها يا بن كوز فإنه غذا الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration “I only call upon my Lord” explains what the preceding clause means by the Prophet calling upon God.
rows.anchor: وجملة { قل إنما أدعو ربي ولا أشرك به أحدا } بيان لجملة { يدعوه }

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most readers use the past-tense qāla, making the statement explain the servant’s act of calling.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { قال } بصيغة الماضي

rows.speaker: حمزة وعاصم وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: Ḥamzah, ʿĀṣim, and Abū Jaʿfar read qul as an imperative; the sentence then begins afresh and continues the revealed instruction.
rows.anchor: وقرأه حمزة وعاصم وأبو جعفر { قل } بدون ألف على صيغة الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the imperative reading, the implied continuation is “it was revealed to me … then say: I call only upon my Lord”; it remains part of the revelation.
rows.anchor: فهو من تمام ما أوحي به إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction means that the Prophet worships no one besides God.
rows.anchor: لا أدعو غيره ، أي لا أعبد غيره دونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added denial of associating anyone with God reinforces the restriction and is separately stated to give it special emphasis.
rows.anchor: تأكيدا لمفهوم القصر ، وأصله أن لا يعطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 21–23 begin a fresh address: after recounting hidden matters about followers and rejecters, the sūra turns to instructing the Prophet how to answer hostile opponents.
rows.anchor: هذا استئناف ابتدائي . وهو انتقال من ذكر ما أوحي به إلى النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra is called al-Muddaththir in tafsīr works and manuscripts; the title describes the Prophet in the state in which he was addressed, or follows the word used in the sūra, as with al-Muzzammil.
rows.anchor: تسمى في كتب التفسير ( سورة المدثر ) وكذلك سميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyyah and al-Qurṭubī report consensus that the sūra is Meccan; al-Itqān does not list it among partly Medinan sūras.
rows.anchor: وهي مكية حكى الاتفاق على ذلك ابن عطية والقرطبي

rows.speaker: محمد بن النقيب المقدسي
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī says Muḥammad ibn al-Naqīb al-Maqdisī reported a view, attributed ambiguously to Muqātil or concerning 74:31 onward, that this passage was revealed in Medina; Ibn ʿĀshūr found no chain or corroboration.
rows.anchor: وذكر الآلوسي أن صاحب ( التحرير ) ( محمد بن النقيب المقدسي المتوفى سنة 698

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: The report from ʿĀʾishah in both Ṣaḥīḥs says the first revelation comprised 96:1–5, followed by a pause, without mentioning any intervening revelation; this supports the view that al-Muddaththir was second.
rows.anchor: في حديث عائشة في ( الصحيحين ) في صفة بدء الوحي

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jābir’s report, transmitted by Abū Salamah through multiple routes and wordings, recounts that after the pause the Prophet heard a heavenly voice, saw the angel from Ḥirāʾ seated between heaven and earth, and returned frightened to Khadījah asking to be covered; some transmissions add that he asked for cold water.
rows.anchor: وكذلك حديث جابر بن عبد الله من رواية أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن من طرق كثيرة وبألفاظ يزيد بعضها على بعض

rows.speaker: النووي
rows.claim: Al-Nawawī explains that pouring cold water on the Prophet was intended to calm his fright.
rows.anchor: قال النووي : صب الماء لتسكين الفزع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the command to the cloaked one to rise and leave impurity, revelation became intense and continued successively.
rows.anchor: ثم حمي الوحي وتتابع اه
